title: Nyingma Gyubum (rnying ma rgyud 'bum, the Collected Tantras of the Ancients)
summary: The canon of Old Tantras not (or only partly) admitted to the Kangyur: the tantras of Atiyoga (mind, space and instruction series, incl. the Seventeen Tantras), Anuyoga (the root sūtras) and Mahāyoga (tantra section and sādhana section), with protector texts. Compiled in its extant form from the 15th c.

attribution.tradition: The tantras were taught by the buddhas of the three kāyas and translated in the first diffusion; Ratna Lingpa (1403-1479) gathered them into a collection.
attribution.scholarly: Several editions (Tingkye, Tsamdrag, Derge, Kathmandu) differ in contents and order; the Derge edition was prepared under Getse Paṇḍita in the late 18th c.

structure.description: Arranged by vehicle: Atiyoga, Anuyoga, Mahāyoga; editions of c. 25-46 volumes (exact counts differ by edition; not recorded here)

notes: Not local. Volume counts omitted deliberately (see REPORT.md).

title: Nyingma Kama (rnying ma bka' ma, the Canonical Transmission)
summary: The collection of the 'spoken word' lineage of the Nyingma: the three inner tantras with their commentaries, empowerment and sādhana texts transmitted without interruption from the first diffusion (as distinct from treasures). Edited at Mindroling by Terdak Lingpa and Lochen Dharmaśrī, and greatly expanded by Dudjom Rinpoche in the 20th c.

title: The Māyājāla (sgyu 'phrul drva ba) cycle of tantras
summary: The family of Mahāyoga tantras of the 'Magical Net' to which the Guhyagarbha belongs: in the Derge Old Tantra section the Guhyagarbha root (Tōh 832), the 'Mirror of All Secrets' (Tōh 833), a longer Guhyagarbha (Tōh 834), the 'Great Magical Net of the Goddess' (Tōh 836) and the 'Great Supreme Uttara' of the Guhyagarbha (Tōh 837). Tradition counts eight Māyājāla tantras (sgyu 'phrul sde brgyad).

notes: Existence and titles checked in the local catalogue (Derge-Kangyur D832-D837); the grouping of eight is from memory.

title: Guhyagarbha Tantra (dpal gsang ba'i snying po de kho na nyid rnam par nges pa)
summary: The root tantra of Mahāyoga in 22 chapters: in Akaniṣṭha the buddhas teach that all phenomena are primordially enlightened, that the aggregates and elements are the male and female buddhas, and set out bodhicitta, the wheel of syllables, the peaceful and wrathful maṇḍalas, empowerment, samaya and the secret instruction. It is the most commented Nyingma tantra (Rongzom, Longchenpa, Lochen Dharmaśrī, Mipham).

attribution.tradition: Taught by Samantabhadra/Vajrasattva; translated by Vimalamitra with Nyak Jñānakumāra and Ma Rinchen Chok (Nyingma histories).
attribution.scholarly: Its Indian origin was contested by 11th-13th c. critics; the Nyingma report a Sanskrit manuscript found at Samye (see dsp:authenticity-of-nyingma-tantras).

scholarly.text: translated by the late 8th-9th c. (cited in early commentaries)

attribution.tradition: Translated, according to its colophon, by the Indian abbot Dharmabodhi, Dānarakṣita and the translator Che btsan skyes from the script of Bruzha, in Bruzha.
attribution.scholarly: Its Gilgit (Bruzha) connection is noted by historians; early Anuyoga lineage via Nupchen Sangye Yeshe.

title: Kunjed Gyalpo (chos thams cad rdzogs pa chen po byang chub kyi sems kun byed rgyal po, the All-Creating King)
summary: The root tantra of the mind series in 84 chapters: bodhicitta, the 'all-creating king', speaks to Vajrasattva in the first person, teaching that everything is its own display, that there is nothing to meditate, no samaya to keep, no ground or path to traverse, and that effort is a sickness; it includes the 'six vajra lines' and other early mind-series scriptures as chapters, and restricts the teaching to fit recipients.

title: Dola Serzhun (rdo la gser zhun, Gold Refined from Ore) = Byang chub kyi sems bsgom pa (Bodhicittabhāvanā), Tōh 2591
summary: Mañjuśrīmitra's verse treatise on cultivating bodhicitta as the non-conceptual path: the awakened mind is beyond conceptual examination and verbal convention, worldly conventions of valid cognition are not needed on this yogic path, and those who seek other paths are 'like gold in ore' — worthy of compassion. One of the five early mind-series translations; preserved in the Tengyur.

title: The eighteen scriptures of the mind series (sems sde bco brgyad)

notes: The thirteen titles are given from memory and may contain errors; list for checking (REPORT.md).

title: The Seventeen Tantras of the Instruction Series (man ngag sde'i rgyud bcu bdun)
summary: The canonical tantras of the innermost secret instruction series (snying thig), taught by Samantabhadra and transmitted via Garab Dorje, Mañjuśrīmitra, Śrī Siṃha and Vimalamitra. They teach the ground, the lamps, the direct introduction, cutting through, direct crossing and its four visions, the bardos and the fruit; the Reverberation of Sound (Dra Thalgyur) is the root.

attribution.tradition: Taught by Samantabhadra; brought to Tibet by Vimalamitra and concealed; recovered by Neten Dangma Lhungyal and passed through Chetsün Senge Wangchuk and Zhangtön.

title: Cig car 'jug pa rnam par mi rtog pa'i bsgom don (The Meaning of Meditation on Non-conceptuality: the Simultaneous Entry), Tōh 3910
summary: A Madhyamaka meditation manual attributed to Vimalamitra on entering non-conceptual samādhi all at once, concluding with the aspiration that all beings gain the eye of wisdom and quickly attain omniscience. Relevant to the Samye-era question of sudden and gradual entry.

attribution.tradition: Colophon: composed by the great master Vimalamitra; translated by Dharmatāśīla and Yeshe De.

title: Samten Migdrön (bsam gtan mig sgron, the Lamp for the Eye in Contemplation)
summary: Nupchen Sangye Yeshe's treatise distinguishing four approaches to contemplation — the gradual (tsen min, of Kamalaśīla), the simultaneous (ston mun, the Chan of Moheyan), Mahāyoga and Atiyoga — ranking each above the last and so distinguishing the Great Perfection from Chan.
notes: Chapter structure not recorded; teachings given at section level (REPORT.md).

title: Tegchen Tsuljug (theg chen tshul 'jug, Entering the Way of the Great Vehicle)
summary: Rongzom Chökyi Zangpo's defence of the Great Perfection view: all appearances are like illusions, established only as appearance; perfect buddhahood is present from the beginning, and appearances are primordially pure.

title: Konchok Drel (rgyud rgyal gsang ba snying po'i 'grel pa dkon cog 'grel)
summary: Rongzom's commentary on the Guhyagarbha, a foundational statement of the 'great purity and equality' view of Mahāyoga.

title: Bashe (sba bzhed / dba' bzhed, the Testament of Ba)
summary: Early Tibetan account of the introduction of Buddhism under Trisong Detsen: the invitations of Śāntarakṣita and Padmasambhava, the building of Samye, the ordination of the first monks and the debate between the Indian and Chinese parties.

scholarly.text: core from the 9th-11th c.; several recensions
